stem: A nurse is caring for an alert client with significant visual impairment. Which communication approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Begin care without identifying yourself, keep the room dim, and provide written instructions in standard print without offering to read them aloud.
options.B: Identify yourself when entering, but reduce room lighting and rely on written information rather than reading pertinent information to the client.
options.C: Provide adequate lighting, but leave important item locations undescribed and avoid reading written information aloud unless the client specifically requests it.
options.D: Identify yourself when entering, provide adequate lighting, read pertinent information aloud, and verbally orient the client to locations of important items as needed.

rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals recommends identifying yourself when entering the space of a client with impaired vision, providing adequate room lighting, reading pertinent information to the client, and identifying item locations. Therefore D is correct. A omits identification, uses inadequate lighting, and withholds oral access to written information. B identifies the nurse but conflicts with the guidance on adequate lighting and reading pertinent information aloud. C provides lighting but omits two other recommended supports: reading pertinent information and orienting the client to item locations.
educational_objective: Choose communication and environmental strategies that help an alert client compensate for visual impairment by identifying the nurse, optimizing lighting, reading pertinent information aloud, and orienting item locations.

source_original.stem: A nurse is caring for an alert client with significant visual impairment. Which communication approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Identify yourself after beginning care, then move personal items as needed without describing the changes because touch will help the client locate them later.
options.B: Use touch to announce your presence and rely mainly on gestures during care because verbal descriptions provide little benefit when vision is impaired.
options.C: Speak primarily to a companion about the environment and procedures because the companion can later explain visual details to the client afterward.
options.D: Identify yourself when entering, provide adequate lighting, read pertinent information aloud, and describe locations of important items verbally as needed.

source_original.rationale: Communication with visual impairment should maximize verbal orientation and accessible information. Option D is correct because the nurse identifies self, provides appropriate lighting, reads pertinent information aloud, and verbally describes item locations. Option A moves belongings without orientation. Option B relies on gestures that the client may not see. Option C unnecessarily redirects communication to a companion rather than the client.
